paragraphs: Help workers recognise bullying, know the difference from reasonable management action, and use the provider's process to raise it.

In this part, what bullying is and is not. Repeated unreasonable behaviour creating a risk to health and safety. Examples: exclusion, intimidation, overloading, humiliation. Reasonable management action carried out reasonably. Single incidents and personality clashes. Read your provider's policy for this topic alongside this course. Completing the course shows you have done the training. It does not by itself guarantee an audit outcome.

title: Understanding Restrictive Practices
description: The Commission's stated top priority is reducing and eliminating restrictive practices. Every worker must recognise all five regulated types, including the ones that hide in daily routines, and know what to do when one is used without authorisation.

In this part, the five types. Seclusion. Chemical restraint including PRN. Mechanical restraint. Physical restraint. Environmental restraint: locked doors, fridges, cupboards, gates.
